attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'if that's all that we saw' antecedent and the predicted skeptical reaction. Leaving out 'wouldn't tell us much' does not change what he committed to.

contract.note: Reading the antecedent as dancing or similar spectacle, with no task demos, is the ordinary reading of 'one more dancing robot'. A broader reading that counts all staged footage as 'canned' could change whether the antecedent was met.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous Reuters report says the event showed video of the robot carrying a box, watering plants and moving bars. This bears on the antecedent, not on the predicted reaction, and shows the dance-only condition did not occur.

reviews.rationale: The early-resolution rule is met: a dated report shows task-oriented footage at the Sept 30, 2022 event, so the dance-only antecedent did not happen. Under policy, a conditional whose antecedent did not occur is not scored. The predicted expert skepticism is not assessed.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: Faithfully restores 'has never been' and 'the real problem'. It is a broad, partly evaluative historical observation.

contract.note: The plain reading (flexible robots in varied settings; 'real problem' as a central continuing obstacle; 'never' as emphatic contrast) is fair and ordinary in context. It does not deny that specialised robots succeed.

evidence.note: SRI's own history of Shakey (1966–72) documents robot demos decades before the post. It is an institutional disclosure but adequate for a historical fact. It is one example, not proof of 'many'.
2021 survey reports poor out-of-distribution performance and a need for robust, safe real-world operation. It is limited to social navigation.
2018 survey documents weeks-long service-robot deployments alongside open challenges in changing environments. This qualifies a demo-only picture without contradicting the robustness point.

reviews.rationale: On the fair plain reading, robot demos go back decades (Shakey), and pre-post research names poor performance in unfamiliar conditions and robust real-world operation as continuing obstacles. Deployment evidence (e3) shows limited real-world success but notes unresolved challenges, so it does not contradict. Support is moderate, with no exhaustive ranking.

reviews.rationale: Nothing in the packet shows Tesla gave an LLM-connected robot demo, so the antecedent's status is unknown, and the early-resolution rule is not met. Under policy, a conditional whose antecedent is unknown is not scored. Expert reactions cannot be assessed without it.
